proof_summary: An explicit evaluation of the continued-fraction recurrence gives a numerator involving \(T(n)=(n+1)^2-5\); when \(T(n)=pm\) with \(n<p\), factorial divisibility and parity show that the denominator cancels exactly the factor \(2m\), while \(p\) cannot cancel, leaving reduced numerator \(p\). Quadratic reciprocity makes \(5\) a square modulo \(p\), so a root \(x\) and the choice \(n=x-1\) ensure \(p\mid T(n)\); the exceptional possibility \(n=6\) is excluded by divisibility, with \(p=11\) handled separately.
